title: SLI trajectory dashboard and initiative synchronization playbook
creator: Aisha Morgan
description: Problem: Teams at Redwood struggle to prioritize reliability initiatives across multiple services because SLI targets and error budget trajectories live in disparate dashboards. We need a product-level artifact that makes trajectory-aware prioritization explicit: a heatmap + tranche assignment for initiatives tied to SLI rolling windows, plus a playbook for synchronizing releases and rollouts with error budget state. This ticket captures scope for a cross-functional deliverable: a SLI Trajectory Dashboard (visual + exportable CSV), a tranche allocator that maps initiatives to error-budget burn rates, and an Initiative Synchronization Playbook that defines cadence, signals, and runbook actions for canary/rollback decisions.
acceptance_criteria: Interactive SLI Trajectory Dashboard prototype available in datadog/dashboard-link and as a read-only Confluence embed
Heatmap view that groups services into 'Stable / At Risk / Critical' based on 30d/7d/1d burn rates and projected time-to-zero error-budget
Tranche allocator algorithm implemented as a lightweight script documented in GitHub (repo: github.com/redwood-inference/slo-tools) that assigns initiatives to tranches and outputs a CSV
Playbook document with explicit decision thresholds, stakeholders, and automation hooks (PagerDuty, Slack channel, console rollback API) published to Confluence
At least one service pilot agrees to use the dashboard and playbook during their next rollout and provides feedback in the pilot retro
success_metrics: Reduction in time-to-rollback for pilot service from detection to action by >= 30%
>80% adoption by reliability owners for initiatives planned in next quarter (self-reported via survey)
Number of surprise outages attributed to unknown error-budget depletion drops by 50% for pilot cohort
deliverables: Confluence playbook (SLO Trajectory & Initiative Sync) with embedded examples
Pilot retro notes and adoption survey results
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (2 weeks): Build prototype dashboard using existing SLI sources and produce CSV export. Phase 2 (2 weeks): Implement tranche allocator and vet algorithm with SREs. Phase 3 (2 weeks): Publish playbook, run 1 pilot with serving-runtime team during a planned rollout. Phase 4 (2 weeks): Iterate on thresholds and automation hooks, prepare for broader rollout next cycle. Communication: weekly brief at Reliability Sync, PRD link in #product-reliability, and a launch announcement during Town Hall if pilot metrics meet targets.
risks: Metric fidelity: SLIs measured differently across services could make projections inaccurate
Over-reliance on projected burn rates may cause unnecessary rollbacks
Automation hooks (rollback API) need careful access control to avoid accidental rollbacks
Resource contention: SREs and runtime engineers are on critical delivery windows
